# Requirements

AGON turns dojo/ from a 10-scenario serial qualification script into a production-grade, scalable, high-accuracy agent-and-model testing STANDARD with a professional, calibrated scoring metric that can be published and cited. The standard is partitioned by system-under-test into THREE suites: (1) Raw Model Performance — the bare model with no tools or scaffolding, isolating intrinsic reasoning/knowledge/instruction-following/calibration; (2) Agentic Performance — model plus the Cody-style agentic scaffolding (tool surface, workspace, verify_run/turn_in done-gate, step budget), the behavior-under-agency tier that today's dojo run_agentic already exercises; (3) Matrix Receptive Agent (MRA) Performance — the composed production agent (main agent + Cassandra modifier agent + cortex memory logger agent), scored by an ablation/differential method (main-only vs main+cassandra vs main+cassandra+cortex) that ATTRIBUTES emergent gains (loop-kill/self-heal, doubt-vs-assurance control, memory continuity) to a specific component instead of asserting them. The immediate driver is Cassandra Round 2: the silent-voice controller must be built and PROVEN in AGON before it touches production, using the two canonical items already identified (deepseek-v4-pro w_broken_gate 22-step spiral = the loop-kill target; mimo-2.5-pro clean 9-step run = the stay-silent baseline). AGON preserves dojo's hard guarantees — competence is post-hoc ground truth never the model's own claim; sanitized VERIFY_PATH plus shim sweeps defeat gate-gaming; hard DQ flags cap a slot regardless of aggregate — and adds what a citable metric requires: a versioned capability taxonomy, a declarative contributable scenario corpus with contamination classes, golden-fixture scorer self-tests, bounded concurrency plus a provider registry, real sandbox isolation, seeded reproducibility with signed provenance-stamped result cards, calibrated confidence-bounded scoring (bootstrap CIs, flake accounting, item-discrimination weighting replacing hand-tuned constants), the AQI headline index with MPI/APS/RAS sub-scores, and a CI promotion gate. This is a spec-only session: plan, author spec.kvx + design.body.md, render via specgen, set active. No implementation or deploy.

## Requirement 1: Versioned capability taxonomy partitioned by the three suites

**User Story:** As the standard owner, I want a documented, versioned capability ontology organized by system-under-test, so that scores roll up defensibly instead of via ad-hoc weights and the standard is legible to outsiders.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE taxonomy SHALL define exactly three suites by system-under-test: Suite 1 Raw Model (bare model, no tools), Suite 2 Agentic (model + Cody-style scaffolding), Suite 3 MRA (main + Cassandra-modifier + cortex-logger composition).
2. EACH suite SHALL enumerate its realms (taxonomy branches) and EACH realm SHALL enumerate leaf capabilities, each leaf carrying a definition, a falsifiable pass condition, difficulty tiers, and a minimum item count.
3. THE taxonomy SHALL be a single versioned source-of-truth artifact under dojo/ (schema-validated), and every scenario SHALL declare the leaf capabilities it probes.
4. A test SHALL prove every scenario in the corpus references only taxonomy leaves that exist, and every leaf meeting the standard's coverage floor has at least its minimum item count.

## Requirement 2: Declarative, contributable, versioned scenario corpus with contamination classes

**User Story:** As a contributor, I want scenarios defined as validated declarative items rather than Python literals, so that the corpus can grow to hundreds of items without becoming unmaintainable or leaking into training sets.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A scenario SHALL be a declarative record with a versioned schema: id, suite, capabilities, difficulty, kind (plain | agentic | mra), seed_source, files, sheet, verify, ground_truth, scorer, sut_config, contamination_class.
2. THE loader SHALL validate every scenario against the schema and reject an unknown field, a missing required field, or a capability not present in the taxonomy.
3. THE corpus SHALL support three families — seeded-from-real (a referenced incident), synthetic-parametric (templated with a per-run randomized instance), and adversarial (a designed trap) — and a contamination_class of public | holdout | rotating.
4. THE existing 10 scenarios SHALL be ported onto the schema with identical observable scoring behavior, and a test SHALL prove the port is behavior-preserving.
5. THE corpus SHALL support canary/holdout leak-detection items (to detect training-set contamination) and synthetic-parametric freshness — each parameterized item SHALL instantiate a fresh, non-repeating instance per run — and a test SHALL prove a parametric item does not repeat its instance across runs.

## Requirement 3: Golden-fixture scorer and verify self-validation

**User Story:** As the standard owner, I want every scorer and verify command proven against known-correct and known-incorrect fixtures, so that a broken scorer can never silently ship and inflate or deflate the metric.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. EACH scenario SHALL declare a golden-correct fixture and a golden-incorrect fixture; a validation pass SHALL assert the scorer scores the correct fixture high and the incorrect fixture low, and that every verify command exits 0 on correct and non-zero on incorrect. FOR polarity-inverted anti-Goodhart/trap items the check SHALL be polarity-aware — the non-gamed fixture SHALL score high and the metric-gaming shortcut SHALL score low.
2. THE validation pass SHALL run as a fast offline check (no model calls) and SHALL be a stop condition when red.
3. A planner/verify-authoring scenario SHALL execute the authored commands against a golden fixture (generalizing today's score_planner golden-dir check) and SHALL detect a structurally-unpassable command.

## Requirement 4: Suite 1 — Raw Model Performance (MPI)

**User Story:** As an evaluator, I want the bare model measured without any agentic scaffolding, so that intrinsic capability is isolated and predicts the ceiling of any agent built on it.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. SUITE 1 SHALL run the model with no tools and no workspace (single or short multi-turn) across realms: reasoning (multi-step arithmetic, algebra, logic puzzles, constraint satisfaction, deductive and inductive entailment), knowledge/factuality (closed-book facts and an anti-hallucination probe with a known-nonexistent answer), instruction-following and strict-format adherence, structured-output conformance (JSON, YAML/CSV, and regex-grammar with nesting/escaping edges), long-context comprehension (needle, multi-needle, distractor resistance, cross-reference, read-full fidelity), calibration/epistemic honesty, refusal/safety, output stability, token economy, multilingual/cross-tokenizer consistency, and adversarial-prompt robustness (prompt-injection, jailbreak, distractor-instruction resistance).
2. SUITE 1 ground truth SHALL use deterministic checkers (exact-match, schema-validation, numeric) wherever an oracle exists, and SHALL NOT score a dimension by keyword-match where a deterministic oracle is available.
3. SUITE 1 SHALL emit a Model Performance Index (MPI) with per-realm sub-scores and confidence intervals.
4. SUITE 1 SHALL include a multilingual/cross-tokenizer realm (the same item across languages/scripts to expose tokenizer bias, scored by a deterministic oracle per variant with a bounded cross-variant gap) and an adversarial-prompt-robustness realm (prompt-injection, jailbreak, and distractor-instruction resistance), each scored by a deterministic predicate paired with a benign control where over-refusal is possible.

## Requirement 5: Suite 2 — Agentic Performance (APS)

**User Story:** As an evaluator, I want behavior-under-agency measured on the real Cody-style tool loop, so that a model's conduct with tools, gates, and budgets is scored on ground truth, not claims.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. SUITE 2 SHALL run the model against the agentic scaffolding (fs tool surface, workspace, verify_run/turn_in engine-enforced done-gate, step budget) across realms: competence, tool mastery and error recovery (including correct tool selection), discipline (bounded loops, budget, read-full, no redundant re-scan), integrity-under-agency, planning/satisfiable-verify, adjudication (reject fake/tautological/trivial tests, accept genuine evidence), adaptivity, scope/safety (protected files, destructive-command restraint, workspace-escape refusal), multi-file/multi-step project tasks (cross-file edits, dependency ordering, build-then-test), in-task state/memory, and anti-Goodhart traps.
2. SUITE 2 competence SHALL be post-hoc ground truth (the harness re-verifies), and the hard DQ flags (gate-gaming, gamed-artifact, scope-violation, fake-accepted) SHALL cap the affected slot at zero regardless of aggregate.
3. SUITE 2 SHALL emit an Agentic Performance Score (APS) with the worker/planner/judge/neo slot scores and confidence intervals.
4. SUITE 2 SHALL include multi-file/multi-step project realms (cross-file edits, dependency ordering, build-then-test pipelines), an in-task state/memory realm (carry a fact established early across many later steps without drift), and anti-Goodhart trap items whose metric-gaming shortcut is polarity-scored to earn a low score.

## Requirement 6: Suite 3 — Matrix Receptive Agent performance by ablation/differential scoring

**User Story:** As the owner, I want the composed MRA measured by ablation, so that every emergent gain is attributed to the Cassandra modifier or the cortex logger by a measured delta rather than asserted.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. SUITE 3 SHALL run each MRA scenario in configured system-under-test variants — at minimum main-only, main+cassandra, and main+cassandra+cortex — and SHALL score the DELTA between variants as the primary product.
2. SUITE 3 realms SHALL include loop-kill/self-heal, doubt-vs-assurance control, guardrail enforcement (content-only, metacognition-only, dual-record audit), memory continuity/cortex fidelity, multi-session continuity (bridged only by cortex), emergent integrity, composition economics (modifier+logger token/latency overhead vs benefit), and negative/no-regression ablations (a component must not degrade a healthy baseline), each measured as an ablation delta with a confidence interval.
3. SUITE 3 SHALL emit a Receptive Agent Score (RAS) reported together with its per-realm ablation deltas; a variant that fails to improve (or regresses) the baseline SHALL be shown as such, never hidden.
4. SUITE 3 SHALL report composition economics (the token/latency overhead of the Cassandra modifier plus the cortex logger weighed against the benefit delta) as a first-class axis, and SHALL include negative/no-regression ablations proving a component does not degrade the healthy baseline; any regression SHALL be surfaced, never hidden.

## Requirement 7: Cassandra silent-voice controller hook + dual-record audit (the Round-2 driver)

**User Story:** As the owner, I want AGON to be the instrument that proves the Cassandra silent-voice controller before production, so that the mechanic is validated on the canonical loop-kill and stay-silent cases.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE agentic run loop SHALL expose a controller hook that, between turns, MAY edit the previous assistant message content in place (touching content only, never tool_calls/roles/tool messages), gated by loop/stall metrics and starting at turn >= 2, at most one modification per turn.
2. EVERY controller modification SHALL be dual-recorded as first-class run artifacts: original_content, cassandra_mod, and trigger; a test SHALL prove no modification ever alters facts (metacognition only) and never touches non-content fields.
3. THE two canonical items SHALL be encoded: the deepseek-v4-pro w_broken_gate 22-step spiral (ended_by=step_budget, integrity 0.0) as the loop-kill target, and the mimo-2.5-pro clean 9-step run as the stay-silent baseline.
4. A test SHALL prove, via the Suite 3 ablation, that enabling the controller kills the loop on the target case (bounded well before the step budget with an honest partial) and stays silent on the healthy baseline (no modification fired).

## Requirement 8: Scale — bounded-concurrency work queue and provider registry

**User Story:** As an operator, I want the gauntlet to run many models x scenarios x reps in parallel within provider limits, so that a full run is minutes not hours.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE runner SHALL execute (model x scenario x rep) units through a bounded-concurrency work queue rather than the current fully-serial loop.
2. THE provider registry SHALL generalize the current MODEL_ROUTES map into pluggable providers, each with its own endpoint, key env, served-model id, completion-budget field, extra body params, per-provider concurrency limit, retry/backoff with cost accounting, and a tools-unsupported fallback per provider (a provider that does not support native tool-calls SHALL degrade to a documented fallback rather than failing).
3. A run SHALL be resumable and re-scorable from cached raw transcripts without re-invoking the model, and a test SHALL prove re-scoring a cached run reproduces identical scores.

## Requirement 9: Real sandbox isolation for exec and verify

**User Story:** As an operator running many and possibly untrusted models, I want workspace exec and verification isolated, so that scaling and untrusted candidates cannot damage the host or contaminate other runs.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WORKSPACE exec and verify_run SHALL execute in an isolated sandbox (container or rootless namespace) with a constrained filesystem and no network by default, preserving the sanitized VERIFY_PATH guarantee.
2. THE shim-sweep and shim-detection anti-gaming guarantees SHALL be preserved under isolation, and a test SHALL prove a poisoned tool shim planted in the workspace cannot reach the verify path.
3. SANDBOX unavailability SHALL degrade to a clearly-labeled reduced-isolation mode rather than silently running unsandboxed.

## Requirement 10: Reproducibility and signed provenance result cards

**User Story:** As an outside party, I want every result reproducible and provenance-stamped, so that a published AGON score can be independently verified and trusted.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. EACH run SHALL emit a result card stamping: model id and served id, harness/standard version, corpus content hash, per-item seeds, temperature policy, per-item raw transcripts, scores, and confidence intervals.
2. THE result card SHALL be integrity-stamped (content hash / signature) so tampering is detectable, and a test SHALL prove a modified card fails verification.
3. GIVEN the same corpus hash, harness version, seeds, and a deterministic-eligible item, re-running SHALL reproduce the deterministic dimensions exactly; non-deterministic dimensions SHALL be reported with variance.

## Requirement 11: Calibrated, confidence-bounded scoring methodology

**User Story:** As the standard owner, I want scoring to be statistically defensible, so that AGON numbers survive scrutiny as an industry metric rather than reading as hand-tuned.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. EACH dimension SHALL be in [0,1] against a published rubric; N reps per item SHALL yield a mean plus bootstrap confidence interval, and flake rate SHALL be reported with API-error runs excluded transparently.
2. REALM and slot weights SHALL be derived by item-discrimination calibration (how well an item separates a reference panel of strong vs weak models), replacing the hand-tuned constants currently in run.py aggregate().
3. HARD DQ flags SHALL remain absolute — they cap the relevant index at zero regardless of aggregate — and adversarial anti-Goodhart items SHALL be part of the corpus.
4. A test SHALL prove the calibration is reproducible from the reference-panel data and that removing a high-discrimination item measurably changes the weights; the calibration SHALL flag dead items (an item that fails to separate the strong from the weak reference panel) so item quality is auditable.

## Requirement 12: The AQI metric — MPI / APS / RAS sub-indices and a headline index

**User Story:** As a consumer of the standard, I want one coherent index with legible sub-scores, so that models and agents can be compared at a glance and in depth.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. AGON SHALL emit an Agent Qualification Index (AQI) composed of the three suite indices — MPI (Suite 1), APS (Suite 2), RAS (Suite 3) — each with confidence intervals and a per-realm profile.
2. THE headline AQI SHALL be a published, documented composition of the sub-indices; the composition formula SHALL live in the standard artifact, not be buried in code.
3. ECONOMICS (tokens, reasoning tokens, wall time, steps, cost) SHALL be a first-class reported axis alongside the quality indices, never hidden.

## Requirement 13: Reporting to the house standard — leaderboard, radar, ablation deltas, cards

**User Story:** As a reader, I want a clear report that shows slot leaderboards, per-realm radar profiles, MRA ablation deltas, and per-run evidence, so that the result is legible and actionable.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE report SHALL render a slot leaderboard, per-realm profiles with confidence intervals, the AQI and its sub-indices, the Suite 3 ablation deltas, an economics table, and a flags section.
2. THE report SHALL link each score to its evidence (raw transcript / post-verify / dual-record audit) so a number is always traceable to what produced it.
3. REPORT copy and any UI SHALL follow the house rules: separation by background-color contrast only (no border strokes for depth), no emojis, no purple/indigo gradients, no glow.

## Requirement 14: CI qualification gate wired to model/agent promotion

**User Story:** As an operator, I want promotion blocked when a candidate regresses against a baseline, so that the $101/hour unqualified-swap incident that motivated dojo cannot recur.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A gate mode SHALL compare a candidate's per-slot/per-suite indices against a stored reference baseline and FAIL promotion on a regression beyond a configured threshold or on any hard DQ flag.
2. THE gate SHALL emit a machine-readable pass/fail verdict plus the human-readable report, and SHALL be runnable as a single command suitable for CI.
3. A test SHALL prove a seeded regressing candidate fails the gate and a seeded non-regressing candidate passes.

## Requirement 15: Published standard and governance

**User Story:** As the standard owner, I want the methodology documented, versioned, and governed, so that AGON can be cited externally and evolve without silently changing what a score means.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE standard SHALL ship a human-readable methodology document (taxonomy, item schema, scoring, AQI composition, contamination policy) generated from or pinned to the versioned source artifacts.
2. THE standard version SHALL be stamped on every result card, and a breaking change to taxonomy/scoring SHALL require a version bump with a migration note.
3. HOLDOUT and rotating scenarios SHALL never be emitted into public artifacts, and a test SHALL prove no holdout item content appears in any published/rendered output.

## Requirement 16: No-fakes end-to-end proof on real models

**User Story:** As the owner, I want the whole instrument validated end to end on real models including the canonical Cassandra pair, so that launch-readiness is proven, not asserted.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. AN end-to-end run SHALL execute all three suites on at least the reference-panel models and produce a complete signed result card and report with no stub/mock/fake anywhere in the scoring path.
2. THE Suite 3 Cassandra proof SHALL run the two canonical items through the ablation and demonstrate loop-kill on the target and silence on the baseline, with the dual-record audit present.
3. THE golden-fixture validation, re-score reproducibility, provenance-tamper, and holdout-leak tests SHALL all be green; NO test in this feature SHALL substitute a fake for a real code path, model, or scored artifact.

## Requirement 17: The working protocol and quality bar as a durable operating contract

**User Story:** As the owner, I want the per-session protocol and the standard's quality bar written into this feature's source of truth, so that every session is worked the same disciplined way.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE spec SHALL carry the per-session protocol (recall + read-full + previous-session handoff -> one eligible task in_progress -> build on real code -> validate against golden fixtures and real models -> green -> mark done + handoff + cortex outcome) as a durable, queryable contract.
2. THE spec SHALL carry the non-negotiable quality bar (publishable/citable grade; no fakes; post-hoc ground truth; reproducible provenance; calibrated confidence-bounded scoring; house UI rules).
3. EVERY task in this feature SHALL be worked under that protocol, and the final checkpoint SHALL attest that it was.
